criteria.expectation: Identifies that CatalogStore.init synchronously reads and JSON-decodes (and sorts) the bundled catalog on the main thread, and that it runs before the first frame because the @StateObject is created when the App/first view is built.

Cites file/line evidence from CatalogStore.swift (the Data(contentsOf:)/JSONDecoder/sort inside init) and TrailCatalogApp.swift (@StateObject store = CatalogStore()), plus the manifest growth (6,200 to 52,000 records, ~2 MB to ~18 MB) and the timing jump between build 141 (~450-510 ms) and build 142 (~2.1-2.3 s).

Reads the timings sensibly: treats the first-launch-after-install and low-battery rows as outliers/context rather than the main signal, and notes the build change coincides with the catalog growth (correlation consistent with, not proof of, the cause).
Recommends moving catalog load/decode off the launch path (e.g. async/detached load after first frame with a placeholder, or a lazier/indexed store such as a database), and re-measuring.
Does not invent specific millisecond savings or claim the fix will reach a particular launch time; any numbers quoted come from the provided timings file and are labeled as such.

States that this is a source review only: no Instruments/xctrace trace, os_signpost or MetricKit data was captured, the catalog.json was not inspected, and the QA frame-count method is coarse; names the measurement needed to confirm.
Does not modify, create or delete any file under the input directory, and does not claim to have built or run the app.
Does not report main-thread synchronous catalog loading (or any other launch-blocking work) as a confirmed defect; recognizes load() runs in .task with decoding in Task.detached and init does no I/O.

Says the improvement is supported only by QA frame-count timings (build 143 about 460-500 ms vs 2.1-2.3 s for 142) and that no trace/Instruments/xctrace was captured, so main-thread cleanliness and time-to-usable-list (not just first placeholder frame) are unverified.

Does not demand a rewrite or architecture change; any extra suggestions (e.g. measuring time to populated list, caching, error handling when decode fails, loading-state UX) are explicitly labeled optional/low priority.
Does not fabricate measurements; quotes timings only from the file.
Does not modify, create or delete any file under the input directory, and does not claim to have built or run the app.
